scope: Targeted primary-source comparison. It does not prove absence of equivalent results or bibliographic priority.
article_claim: Explicit certificate and total-trial bounds for existing halving/doubling FW/AFW; an optimal pointwise gap envelope with attaining objectives; zero-base face structure and finite AFW termination with separated initialization lag. No new algorithm, optimal oracle complexity, universal practical superiority or absolute-priority claim.
queries: Primary-reference follow-up from Auto-Conditioned FW and Adaptive Conditional Gradient Sliding
Frank-Wolfe finite termination weak sharp minima active-set identification
function-dependent smoothness exact gradient norm inequality

sources.checked: H0,H1 definition; convex gradient analysis; related work
sources.conclusion: The loss-suboptimality Hessian model is prior. Its gradient-method results are not an LMO stopping theorem.
Two-regime deterministic gradient-descent complexity under the same smoothness model is prior. Phases alone are not a new contribution.

sources.checked: Algorithms 1-2; Theorems 1,3,4 and associated proof identities
sources.conclusion: Quadratic backtracking, total-trial telescoping, averaged-gradient Fenchel certificates and local-curvature AFW geometric progress are prior. The scalar tangent envelope cannot simply be identified with their dual.

sources.checked: Model assumptions; Theorem 5.1; two-regime statements in Table 1
sources.conclusion: Gradient-norm dependent FW and adaptive generalized smoothness are prior. A direct global substitution retains a largest-gradient contribution.
Native comparator uses a compulsory initial LMO move and one charged trial per outer iteration; global gradient-Lipschitz assumption is stronger than the exponential objectives used empirically.

sources.checked: Related-work lag discussion; Section 3 gradient-difference/backtracking strategy; Theorems 4.4-4.5
sources.conclusion: The motivation of slow downward curvature adaptation is explicit prior work. Their stated constrained rates retain global smoothness/gradient constants and concern a different initialization strategy.
A line-search-free composite conditional-gradient method and nonconvex minimum-gap guarantee precede the article.

Count inner LMOs separately from accelerated outer iterations. The stated restart theorem uses local strong convexity and smoothness parameters in its schedule; it cannot be applied from the Hessian assumption alone. No superiority over sliding is claimed.

sources.checked: Relative-smooth kernel and segment-scaling assumptions; Euclidean specialization
sources.conclusion: Adaptive Bregman FW is a broader prior framework. A single global Euclidean substitution is weaker; more suitable kernels or refined consequences are not ruled out.
Uniform extended-curvature and vertex-error-bound AFW rates are prior; the stated theorem uses exact search or a short step.
Polytope scaling, HEB implications, burn-in, computable stopping and adaptive restart rates are prior. The stated restart result uses global away curvature.
Linear objective- and FW-gap convergence outside global gradient smoothness is prior for log-homogeneous barriers, using exact search or local Hessian information.
The quadratic-descent two-branch gap inversion is prior. The article uses a source-dependent local curvature bound and does not claim a new general inversion.

Function-value Hessian bounds and transformed-potential self-bounding precede the affine warm-up model. Its displayed gradient bound uses rho(value)^2 times an integral of 1/rho; our affine-class ray comparison yields exact polynomial constants.

sources.checked: Assumption 1.1; Corollary 1; Appendix A.3 proof and citation of 2022 Lemma 11
sources.conclusion: General second-order self-bounding regularity is prior. Corollary 1 gives the log-enlarged affine-model gradient bound; it does not provide our constrained LMO gap envelope. No general self-bounding principle is claimed new.

Finite active-set identification and maximal away deletions near a strictly complementary solution are prior. Our zero-base model forces the entire solution set to be the exposed face and supplies an objective-level neighborhood and inherited-curvature trial count.

Finite vertex convergence and optimal-face identification with line-search FW variants are prior. We do not claim the general finite-identification phenomenon or that identifying a face solves a nonconstant function on it.

attribution_correction: Earlier wording attributing introduction of function-value Hessian bounds to the warm-up paper was too narrow. The focused article now cites the prior 2022 and 2025 self-bounding frameworks.
